hook: We want to **live together** without marrying.

slides.title: The DV Act **recognises** it.
slides.body: The Domestic Violence Act covers a "relationship in the nature of marriage", alongside marriage, between two people who live or have lived together in a shared household.
slides.ref: Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act 2005 · Sec 2(f)

slides.title: But **not every** live-in counts.
slides.body: The Supreme Court has said Parliament recognised this social change through the DV Act. But not all live-in relationships amount to a relationship in the nature of marriage.
slides.ref: Supreme Court · D. Velusamy v D. Patchaiammal (2010), paras 22, 34, 37

slides.title: When does it **qualify?**
list: You present yourselves to society as like spouses
Both of legal age to marry
Otherwise qualified to marry, incl. being unmarried
Lived together voluntarily for a significant time
slides.ref: Supreme Court · D. Velusamy v D. Patchaiammal (2010), para 33

slides.title: Facing domestic violence? **What she can ask for.**
list: Right not to be pushed out of the shared home
slides.ref: Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act 2005 · Sec 18, 19, 20, 22

slides.title: Where to **apply?**
slides.body: She, a Protection Officer or anyone on her behalf can apply to the **Magistrate.** She can also complain against relatives of the male partner.
slides.ref: Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act 2005 · Sec 12(1), Sec 2(q) proviso

slides.title: Uttarakhand: **you must register.**
slides.body: Couples staying in Uttarakhand, and Uttarakhand residents living elsewhere in India, must register by submitting a statement of live-in relationship to the Registrar. Scheduled Tribes are excluded.
slides.ref: UCC Rules, Uttarakhand, 2025 · Rule 2, Rule 15(3)(b); UCC 2024 · Sec 381

slides.title: Uttarakhand: ending it? **Tell the Registrar.**
slides.body: When partners jointly submit a statement of termination, the Registrar issues both of them a termination certificate within 15 days.
slides.ref: UCC Rules, Uttarakhand, 2025 · Rule 6(5)(e)(i); UCC 2024 · Sec 384

sources: Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005 – Sections 2(a), 2(f), 2(q), 12, 18, 19, 20, 22
Supreme Court of India – D. Velusamy v. D. Patchaiammal, Crl. Appeal Nos. 2028-2029 of 2010 (21 Oct 2010)
Uniform Civil Code, Uttarakhand, 2024 – Sections 381, 384, and Uniform Civil Code Rules, Uttarakhand, 2025 – Rules 2, 6, 15 (ucc.uk.gov.in)
caption:
Living together without marriage? Here's what the law says. 👇

1️⃣ The Domestic Violence Act, 2005 covers a "relationship in the nature of marriage" between partners who share a household
2️⃣ The Supreme Court has said not every live-in relationship qualifies
3️⃣ It looks at whether you present yourselves as like spouses, are of legal age, are otherwise qualified to marry (incl. unmarried), and lived together voluntarily for a significant time
4️⃣ A woman in such a relationship who faces domestic violence can seek protection, residence, monetary relief and compensation from the Magistrate
⚠️ In Uttarakhand, live-in couples must register with the Registrar under the State's Uniform Civil Code, 2024 (Scheduled Tribes excluded)

Source: Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005 (Sec 2, 12, 18, 19, 20, 22); Supreme Court, D. Velusamy v. D. Patchaiammal (2010); Uniform Civil Code Rules, Uttarakhand, 2025 (Rule 15)
